title: Private package fetching (PIR)
description: Private Information Retrieval lets a client fetch a package from a mirror without the mirror learning which package was fetched. The client queries in a way that hides the index — the mirror does more work, but your dependency list stays yours. The defense against dependency-confusion surveillance.
method: PIR query over the package index; the server processes the whole database per query; the client extracts its package; the server learns nothing about the choice.
usage: Use for sensitive dependency fetches; batch queries to amortize server cost.

demo.code:
print('PIR fetch: package #8812 of 1M')
print('mirror processed 1M entries; learned: nothing about #8812')

title: Lockfile hash verification
description: The lockfile pins exact versions and content hashes; the resolver verifies every downloaded artifact against the lockfile before use. Even a compromised mirror can't substitute code — the hash won't match. The lockfile is the trust anchor; the registry is just a dumb byte store.
method: Verify SHA-512 (or better) per artifact at install; fail closed on mismatch; commit lockfiles; review lockfile diffs.
usage: Verify hashes in CI and on developer machines; treat hash mismatches as security incidents.

demo.code:
import hashlib
expected = hashlib.sha256(b'pkg-bytes').hexdigest()
print('download hash:', expected[:12], '== lockfile:', expected[:12], '-> INSTALL')

title: Typosquat detection
description: Attackers publish 'lodahs' next to 'lodash'; typosquat detectors compare new package names against popular ones (edit distance, confusables) and flag or block near-misses. Combined with popularity thresholds (new packages with famous-like names need review), it catches the oldest supply-chain trick.
method: Compute name similarity to popular packages; flag confusables; require review for suspicious new names.
usage: Run on every new package entering the mirror; block automatic mirroring of flagged names.

demo.code:
print('new package "lodahs": edit distance 1 from "lodash" (10M downloads)')
print('FLAGGED: typosquat suspected -> manual review required')

title: Provenance attestation for packages
description: SLSA provenance for packages records where and how each artifact was built; the resolver verifies provenance before installing. A package without valid provenance — built who-knows-where — is rejected. Provenance turns 'this tarball' into 'this tarball built by this CI from this source'.
method: Publishers emit SLSA provenance; resolvers verify it; policies require provenance level thresholds.
usage: Require provenance for critical dependencies; verify in the install pipeline.

demo.code:
print('lodash@4.17.21: provenance SLSA L3 (builder: github-actions, source: lodash/lodash@a1b2)')
print('verified -> INSTALL; no provenance -> REJECT')

title: Dependency firewall rules
description: Like a network firewall for packages: rules specifying which registries, versions, licenses, and publishers are allowed, enforced at resolve time. 'Only these publishers, only these licenses, nothing unpublished in the last 24h' — policy as code for the supply chain.
method: Write allow/deny rules; enforce in the resolver/proxy; log decisions; review rule hits.
usage: Start permissive with logging, tighten based on hits; review the rules quarterly.

demo.code:
rules = ['allow: registry.internal', 'deny: license=GPL', 'deny: age<24h']
print('rules:', rules)
print('request lodash (MIT, 5y old, internal): ALLOW')

title: Offline build verification
description: Verify the build works with zero network: run the full build in a network-namespaced sandbox and confirm success. If the build secretly phones home (for a dependency, a license check, telemetry), the sandbox exposes it — offline verification proves the dependency closure is complete and honest.
method: Build in a no-network namespace; require success; log any blocked connection attempts as findings.
usage: Run offline builds in CI; investigate every blocked connection.

demo.code:
print('build in netns (no network): SUCCESS')
print('blocked attempts: 0 -> dependency closure complete and honest')

title: Namespace-scoped registries
description: Registries support scopes (@acme/*) mapped to specific registry URLs; the resolver never consults the public registry for scoped names. Scoping is the simple, effective confusion defense — private names live in a namespace the public internet can't claim.
method: Configure scope -> registry mappings; enforce at the resolver; audit that no private name resolves publicly.
usage: Scope all private packages; enforce mappings in CI; audit for scope leaks.

demo.code:
print('scopes: @acme/* -> registry.acme.internal')
print('@acme/auth resolves ONLY via internal registry')

title: Air-gapped dependency vendoring
description: The strongest isolation: vendor all dependencies into the repo (or a versioned bundle) on a connected machine, then build air-gapped from the vendor directory. No network resolution at build time means no exfiltration, no confusion, no MITM — the build's inputs are exactly the vendored bytes.
method: Vendor on a trusted machine; verify hashes; build offline from vendor/; the build never touches the network.
usage: Use for the most sensitive builds; re-vendor deliberately, not continuously.

demo.code:
print('vendor/: 142 packages, hashes verified')
print('build --offline: 0 network calls -> SUCCESS (air-gapped)')
